<p>The HUD typically consists of the user's <a href="/w/Health" title="Health">health</a>, <a href="/w/Hunger" class="mw-redirect" title="Hunger">hunger</a>, and <a href="/w/Experience" title="Experience">experience</a> bars, the hotbar, as well as a crosshair that designates the currently focused on block or entity if the player is not playing on a mobile device and has not enabled split controls. The <a href="/w/Armor" title="Armor">armor</a> condition bar appears above the health bar if the player is wearing armor, and the <a href="/w/Damage#Drowning" title="Damage">breath</a> meter displays above the hunger bar if the player's air supply unit is below 300.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>note 1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Note that in the mobile versions of <i>Bedrock Edition</i>, the health and armor bars are on the top left and the hunger and oxygen bars are on the top right. The "<a href="/w/Settings#Video" title="Settings">UI Profile</a>" option under the video settings can be set to "Classic" mode to match <i>Java Edition</i> style.
</p><p>In <a href="/w/Creative" title="Creative">Creative</a> mode, the health, hunger, oxygen, experience, and armor bars are hidden.
</p>

</li>
</ol></div>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Hotbar">Hotbar</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?section=2&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Hotbar" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?action=edit&section=2" title="Edit section's source code: Hotbar"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size pixel-image" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/w/File:Hotbar.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="/images/thumb/Hotbar.png/300px-Hotbar.png?348ad" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="300" height="36" class="mw-file-element" srcset="/images/Hotbar.png?348ad 2x" data-file-width="364" data-file-height="44"></a><figcaption>The hotbar</figcaption></figure>
<figure class="mw-default-size pixel-image" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/w/File:Hotbar_(BE).png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="/images/thumb/Hotbar_%28BE%29.png/300px-Hotbar_%28BE%29.png?84e9b" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="300" height="33" class="mw-file-element" srcset="/images/Hotbar_%28BE%29.png?84e9b 2x" data-file-width="404" data-file-height="44"></a><figcaption>The hotbar in <a href="/w/Bedrock_Edition" title="Bedrock Edition"><i>Bedrock Edition</i></a> when using touch controls</figcaption></figure>
<p>The hotbar is a selection bar that appears on the bottom of the screen. It is where the player stores and selects commonly used <a href="/w/Items" class="mw-redirect" title="Items">items</a>. It consists of the bottom nine slots within the player's inventory. When the player switches an item in hand by <span class="pixel-image" typeof="mw:File"><a href="/w/File:Scroll_wheel.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="/images/Scroll_wheel.png?90ac0" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="24" height="24" class="mw-file-element" data-file-width="16" data-file-height="16"></a></span> Scroll Wheel or <kbd class="key nowrap">1-9</kbd>, its name is shown above the experience level for a short period of time. In <a href="/w/Java_Edition" title="Java Edition"><i>Java Edition</i></a>, this name appears in italics, while in <a href="/w/Bedrock_Edition" title="Bedrock Edition"><i>Bedrock Edition</i></a>, the text has a black background and also shows <a href="/w/Enchantments" class="mw-redirect" title="Enchantments">enchantments</a> of the selected item, and contents of a <a href="/w/Shulker_Box" title="Shulker Box">shulker box</a>. The background opacity can be adjusted with the "Text Background Opacity" option in the <a href="/w/Settings#Accessibility" title="Settings">accessibility settings</a>.
</p><p>Players can <a href="/w/Dual_wield" title="Dual wield">dual wield</a> allowing a second item to be shown on the other side, along with an additional hotbar slot on the same side.‌<sup class="nowrap Inline-Template" title="">[<i><span title="This statement only applies to Java Edition"><a href="/w/Java_Edition" title="Java Edition">JE</a>  only</span></i>]</sup> Both the slot and the item are shown only if it contains an item, which can either be added using the <a href="/w/GUI" class="mw-redirect" title="GUI">GUI</a> or by pressing "<span class="explain" title="Defaults to F on keyboard.">swap items</span>".
</p><p>In <a href="/w/Bedrock_Edition" title="Bedrock Edition"><i>Bedrock Edition</i></a>, the hotbar has an additional button for the inventory when using touch controls. On the <a href="/w/New_Nintendo_3DS_Edition" title="New Nintendo 3DS Edition">New Nintendo 3DS Edition</a>, the hotbar is located on the "Touch Screen" and is slightly different.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Hand">Hand</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?section=3&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Hand" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?action=edit&section=3" title="Edit section's source code: Hand"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>The player's hand is always shown on the right side of the screen (left side if the player's main hand is set to "left"),‌<sup class="nowrap Inline-Template" title="">[<i><span title="This statement only applies to Java Edition"><a href="/w/Java_Edition" title="Java Edition">JE</a>  only</span></i>]</sup> and corresponds to the player's hand in the <a href="/w/Skin" title="Skin">skin</a>. In <a href="/w/Bedrock_Edition" title="Bedrock Edition"><i>Bedrock Edition</i></a>, all animations from the hand as seen in third person are also seen on the HUD, including the breathing animation and eating/drinking. When an item in the hotbar is selected, it shows in place of the hand rotated similarly to held items in third-person, with a switching animation. Some held items can show animations, and when charging a <a href="/w/Crossbow" title="Crossbow">crossbow</a> in <i>Bedrock Edition</i>, the left hand can also be seen. Items can also be held in the <a href="/w/Offhand" class="mw-redirect" title="Offhand">offhand</a> slot, which will show on the other side, but an empty hand is not shown. With <a href="/w/Vibrant_Visuals" title="Vibrant Visuals">Vibrant Visuals</a>, directional light effects (shadows, caustics, light) are also visible on the hand, and held items apply their texture sets.
</p><p>The hand can be toggled independently from the HUD in <i>Bedrock Edition</i>, meaning that it can be shown standalone without other HUD elements. However, pressing <kbd class="key nowrap">F1</kbd> still hides the hand. 
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Locator_bar">Locator bar</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?section=4&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Locator bar" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?action=edit&section=4" title="Edit section's source code: Locator bar"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">Main article: <a href="/w/Locator_Bar" title="Locator Bar">Locator Bar</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size pixel-image" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/w/File:Survival_Locator_Bar.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="/images/thumb/Survival_Locator_Bar.png/300px-Survival_Locator_Bar.png?4f761" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="300" height="26" class="mw-file-element" srcset="/images/thumb/Survival_Locator_Bar.png/600px-Survival_Locator_Bar.png?4f761 2x" data-file-width="728" data-file-height="64"></a><figcaption>Locator bar in <a href="/w/Survival" title="Survival">Survival</a> mode</figcaption></figure>
<p>The locator bar appears in place of the experience bar, except when gaining <a href="/w/XP" class="mw-redirect" title="XP">XP</a>. It shows the position of other <a href="/w/Player" title="Player">players</a> in <a href="/w/Multiplayer" title="Multiplayer">multiplayer</a> as colored square indicators, often referred to as waypoints. They appear approximately within 120° of the camera facing towards the target. If the target is on a significantly different Y-level, an arrow pointing to the target vertically appears over the square indicator.
</p><p>The <a href="/w/Color_code" class="mw-redirect" title="Color code">color</a> of a waypoint is randomly assigned to a player when they join a multiplayer game, or when a waypoint is tracked for the entity; it may also be assigned by their <a href="/w/Team" class="mw-redirect" title="Team">team</a> color. In <i>Java Edition</i>, it can be customized using the <code><span>/<a href="/w/Commands/waypoint" title="Commands/waypoint">waypoint</a></span></code> command.
</p><p>The locator bar can be toggled by the <code><a href="/w/Game_rule#locatorBar" title="Game rule">locatorBar</a></code> game rule. In <i>Java Edition</i>, entities in the locator bar may be tracked if <code><a href="/w/Attribute#waypoint_transmit_range" title="Attribute">waypoint_transmit_range</a></code> attribute is set.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Crosshair">Crosshair</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?section=5&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Crosshair" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?action=edit&section=5" title="Edit section's source code: Crosshair"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>The crosshair is a small cross in the middle of the screen. It shows the aim point of the <a href="/w/Tool" title="Tool">tool</a> or <a href="/w/Item" title="Item">item</a> being held to entities or blocks for attacking or any interactions within a specific <a href="/w/Interaction_range" title="Interaction range">range</a> from the player. The crosshair inverts the colors of the area it is upon, which can result in a nearly invisible crosshair if the area is a medium gray. The crosshair is only shown on touch devices when the control mode is set to "Joystick & aim crosshair", or when the "Split Controls" option is enabled.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Chat">Chat</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?section=6&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Chat" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?action=edit&section=6" title="Edit section's source code: Chat"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">Main article: <a href="/w/Chat" title="Chat">Chat</a></div>
<p>Chat messages are also shown on the HUD, in the bottom left corner‌<sup class="nowrap Inline-Template" title="">[<i><span title="This statement only applies to Java Edition"><a href="/w/Java_Edition" title="Java Edition">Java Edition</a>  only</span></i>]</sup>/top left corner‌<sup class="nowrap Inline-Template" title="">[<i><span title="This statement only applies to Bedrock Edition"><a href="/w/Bedrock_Edition" title="Bedrock Edition">Bedrock Edition</a>  only</span></i>]</sup>, showing anything recently spoken or commands recently executed. In <a href="/w/Java_Edition" title="Java Edition"><i>Java Edition</i></a>, this can be expanded with <kbd class="key nowrap">T</kbd>, allowing the player to enter chat messages or commands, and view the full chat history. In <a href="/w/Bedrock_Edition" title="Bedrock Edition"><i>Bedrock Edition</i></a>, pressing <kbd class="key nowrap">T</kbd> opens the chat menu, which is not part of the HUD but a separate <a href="/w/Menu_screen" title="Menu screen">menu screen</a>.
</p><p>Elements such as the chat size, background opacity, its visibility in general, font, text color, and more can be changed in the <a href="/w/Options" title="Options">options</a>‌<sup class="nowrap Inline-Template" title="">[<i><span title="This statement only applies to Java Edition"><a href="/w/Java_Edition" title="Java Edition">Java Edition</a>  only</span></i>]</sup>/<a href="/w/Chat#Chat_settings" title="Chat">chat settings</a>.‌<sup class="nowrap Inline-Template" title="">[<i><span title="This statement only applies to Bedrock Edition"><a href="/w/Bedrock_Edition" title="Bedrock Edition">Bedrock Edition</a>  only</span></i>]</sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Closed_captions">Closed captions</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?section=7&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Closed captions" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?action=edit&section=7" title="Edit section's source code: Closed captions"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">Main article: <a href="/w/Closed_captions" title="Closed captions">Closed captions</a></div>
<p>Closed captions display text for <a href="/w/Sounds" class="mw-redirect" title="Sounds">sounds</a> in-game. When turned on, this lists sounds in the world that are nearby to the player on the right of the screen. If the sounds are offscreen, "<" or ">" point in the direction the sound is coming from. As the sound fades away, the text also fades, becoming less white.
</p><p>Subtitles can be enabled in the "Music & Sounds"‌<sup class="nowrap Inline-Template" title="">[<i><span title="This statement only applies to Java Edition"><a href="/w/Java_Edition" title="Java Edition">JE</a>  only</span></i>]</sup> or "Accessibility Settings" sections of the <a href="/w/Options" title="Options">options</a>/<a href="/w/Settings" title="Settings">settings</a> menu.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Effects">Effects</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?section=8&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Effects" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?action=edit&section=8" title="Edit section's source code: Effects"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">Main article: <a href="/w/Effect" title="Effect">Effect</a></div>
<p>All <a href="/w/Effect" title="Effect">effects</a> (other than effects with <code>hideParticles</code>, including <a href="/w/Darkness" title="Darkness">Darkness</a> from the warden<sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>) the player currently has are shown on the top-right of the screen. Effects that run out sooner appear farther to the left, and effects that are about to run out start to flash. Additionally, positive effects are shown on the top, and other effects (neutral or negative) are shown on the bottom. Beacon effects have a blue (instead of gray) outline, and effects with particles hidden are not indicated in the HUD.
</p>

<figure class="mw-default-size pixel-image" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/w/File:Horse_jump_bar_empty.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="/images/thumb/Horse_jump_bar_empty.png/300px-Horse_jump_bar_empty.png?b2f78" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="300" height="8" class="mw-file-element" srcset="/images/Horse_jump_bar_empty.png?b2f78 2x" data-file-width="364" data-file-height="10"></a><figcaption>The empty jump bar/dash bar</figcaption></figure> 
<figure class="mw-default-size pixel-image" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/w/File:Horse_jump_bar_full.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="/images/thumb/Horse_jump_bar_full.png/300px-Horse_jump_bar_full.png?8f548" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="300" height="8" class="mw-file-element" srcset="/images/Horse_jump_bar_full.png?8f548 2x" data-file-width="364" data-file-height="10"></a><figcaption>The full jump bar/dash bar</figcaption></figure>
<p>Upon mounting a <a href="/w/Horse" title="Horse">horse</a>, <a href="/w/Donkey" title="Donkey">donkey</a>, <a href="/w/Mule" title="Mule">mule</a>, <a href="/w/Llama" title="Llama">llama</a>, <a href="/w/Pig" title="Pig">pig</a>, <a href="/w/Strider" title="Strider">strider</a>, <a href="/w/Camel" title="Camel">camel</a>, <a href="/w/Happy_ghast" class="mw-redirect" title="Happy ghast">happy ghast</a>, <a href="/w/Nautilus" title="Nautilus">nautilus</a>, or <a href="/w/Zombie_nautilus" class="mw-redirect" title="Zombie nautilus">zombie nautilus</a>, the ridden mob's health bar appears above the hunger bar. It uses a slightly different heart texture than the player's health bar, with them made to resemble saddles.
</p><p>Also, upon mounting a horse, camel, nautilus, or zombie nautilus, the jump bar (for horses) or the dash bar (for camels, nautiluses and zombie nautiluses) also appears above the experience bar. When riding a <a href="/w/Skeleton_horse" class="mw-redirect" title="Skeleton horse">skeleton horse</a> underwater, the oxygen bar, if necessary, appears above the mob health bar.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Action_bar">Action bar</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?section=10&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Action bar" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?action=edit&section=10" title="Edit section's source code: Action bar"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">Main article: <a href="/w/Action_bar" title="Action bar">Action bar</a></div>
<p>The action bar is a space just above the player's hotbar where text can be displayed. Some gameplay elements, such as <a href="/w/Jukeboxes" class="mw-redirect" title="Jukeboxes">jukeboxes</a>, use this to give contextual hints to the player. Text can also be displayed here using the <code><span>/<a href="/w/Commands/title" title="Commands/title">title</a></span></code> command. In <a href="/w/Bedrock_Edition" title="Bedrock Edition"><i>Bedrock Edition</i></a>, the opacity of the black background of the action bar can be adjusted with the "Action Bar Background Opacity" option in the <a href="/w/Settings#Accessibility" title="Settings">accessibility settings</a>.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Autosave_indicator">Autosave indicator</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?section=11&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Autosave indicator" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?action=edit&section=11" title="Edit section's source code: Autosave indicator"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">Main article: <a href="/w/Autosave" title="Autosave">Autosave</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/w/File:Auto_save.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="/images/Auto_save.png?5fbd8" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="162" height="30" class="mw-file-element" data-file-width="162" data-file-height="30"></a><figcaption>The autosave indicator in <a href="/w/Bedrock_Edition" title="Bedrock Edition"><i>Bedrock Edition</i></a>.</figcaption></figure>
<p>The autosave indicator indicates when the game is autosaving. In <i><a href="/w/Java_Edition" title="Java Edition">Java Edition</a></i>, this is turned on by default and shows "Saving world" in the bottom-right of the screen. In <i><a href="/w/Bedrock_Edition" title="Bedrock Edition">Bedrock Edition</a></i>, this is turned off by default and shows an animation of an arrow pointing into a <a href="/w/Chest" title="Chest">chest</a> in the top-right of the screen.
</p><p>Whether or not this appears can be toggled in the <a href="/w/Options" title="Options">options</a>.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Bossbar">Bossbar</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?section=12&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Bossbar" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?action=edit&section=12" title="Edit section's source code: Bossbar"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">Main article: <a href="/w/Bossbar" title="Bossbar">Bossbar</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/w/File:Bossbar_enderdragon.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="/images/thumb/Bossbar_enderdragon.png/300px-Bossbar_enderdragon.png?0d51e" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="300" height="30" class="mw-file-element" srcset="/images/thumb/Bossbar_enderdragon.png/600px-Bossbar_enderdragon.png?0d51e 2x" data-file-width="750" data-file-height="75"></a><figcaption>The bossbar for the <a href="/w/Ender_dragon" class="mw-redirect" title="Ender dragon">ender dragon</a>.</figcaption></figure>
<p>A bossbar is a bar at the top of the screen that can track <a href="/w/Health" title="Health">health</a> of a <a href="/w/Mob#Boss_mobs" title="Mob">boss mob</a> or the total health of <a href="/w/Raid" title="Raid">raid</a> mobs. The bossbar appears naturally in the game through three means: during a <a href="/w/Raid" title="Raid">raid</a>, after constructing a <a href="/w/Wither" title="Wither">wither</a>, and upon entering <a href="/w/The_End" title="The End">the End</a> if the <a href="/w/Ender_dragon" class="mw-redirect" title="Ender dragon">ender dragon</a> has not yet been defeated. In <a href="/w/Java_Edition" title="Java Edition"><i>Java Edition</i></a>, a bossbar can be created manually using the <code>/<a href="/w/Commands/bossbar" title="Commands/bossbar">bossbar</a></code> command. There is a limit of 6<sup class="nowrap Inline-Template" title="">[<i><a href="/w/Special:TalkPage/Heads-up_display" title="Special:TalkPage/Heads-up display"><span title="">verify</span></a></i>]</sup> bars shown.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Screen_effects_and_overlays">Screen effects and overlays</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?section=13&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Screen effects and overlays" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?action=edit&section=13" title="Edit section's source code: Screen effects and overlays"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">Main article: <a href="/w/Screen_effects" title="Screen effects">Screen effects</a></div>
<p>Screen effects encompass a variety of effects applied alongside or beneath the heads-up display as augmentations to the <a href="/w/Player" title="Player">player</a>'s point of view as a method of conveying further information about a player's current state.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Screen_title">Screen title</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?section=14&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Screen title" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?action=edit&section=14" title="Edit section's source code: Screen title"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">Main article: <a href="/w/Commands/title" title="Commands/title">Commands/title</a></div>
<p>A screen title is displayed to players as a single line of large center-aligned text in the middle of their displays, and can include a subtitle; a second, separate line of text displayed just below the title. It is controlled with the <code>/title</code> and <code>/titleraw</code> commands. In <a href="/w/Bedrock_Edition" title="Bedrock Edition"><i>Bedrock Edition</i></a>, the opacity of the black background of the screen title can be adjusted with the "Text Background Opacity" option in the <a href="/w/Settings#Accessibility" title="Settings">accessibility settings</a>.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Scoreboard">Scoreboard</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?section=15&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Scoreboard" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?action=edit&section=15" title="Edit section's source code: Scoreboard"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">Main article: <a href="/w/Scoreboard" title="Scoreboard">Scoreboard</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/w/File:Scoreboard_BE.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="/images/thumb/Scoreboard_BE.png/300px-Scoreboard_BE.png?153cf" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="300" height="81" class="mw-file-element" srcset="/images/thumb/Scoreboard_BE.png/600px-Scoreboard_BE.png?153cf 2x" data-file-width="774" data-file-height="210"></a><figcaption>The scoreboard on the HUD</figcaption></figure>
<p>The scoreboard system is a complex gameplay mechanic utilized through <a href="/w/Commands" title="Commands">commands</a>. Mainly intended for mapmakers and <a href="/w/Server" title="Server">server</a> operators, scoreboards are used to track, set, and list the scores of <a href="/w/Entities" class="mw-redirect" title="Entities">entities</a> in a myriad of different ways. It is displayed on the right side of the screen.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Toasts">Toasts</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?section=16&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Toasts" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?action=edit&section=16" title="Edit section's source code: Toasts"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">Main articles: <a href="/w/Toasts" title="Toasts">Toasts</a> and <a href="/w/Tutorial_hints" title="Tutorial hints">Tutorial hints</a></div>
<p>Toasts are text boxes shown when the player unlocks new <a href="/w/Recipe" class="mw-disambig" title="Recipe">crafting recipes</a>. Additionally, in <a href="/w/Java_Edition" title="Java Edition"><i>Java Edition</i></a>, exclusive toasts show when a new music track starts playing, or the player obtains <a href="/w/Advancement" title="Advancement">advancements</a>. Most of them show up in the top right corner of the screen, and are displayed in front of effect icons. Music toasts appear in the top left of the screen instead.
</p><p>Tutorial hints (also known as game tips in <i><a href="/w/Bedrock_Edition" title="Bedrock Edition">Bedrock Edition</a></i>) are toasts which show up when a player starts a world in <a href="/w/Survival_mode" class="mw-redirect" title="Survival mode">Survival mode</a> for the first time on a device. They are meant to guide new players who may not know the controls. These can be turned off in the <a href="/w/Settings" title="Settings">settings</a>.‌<sup class="nowrap Inline-Template" title="">[<i><span title="This statement only applies to Bedrock Edition"><a href="/w/Bedrock_Edition" title="Bedrock Edition">Bedrock Edition</a>  only</span></i>]</sup>
</p><p>If multiple recipes are unlocked at once, they all use the same toast. If multiple advancements are unlocked at once, they appear listed one under the other. Up to five toasts can be displayed at once.
</p><p>In <a href="/w/Bedrock_Edition" title="Bedrock Edition"><i>Bedrock Edition</i></a>, the duration of toast messages can be adjusted in the <a href="/w/Settings#Accessibility" title="Settings">accessibility settings</a>.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Demo_timer">Demo timer</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?section=17&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Demo timer" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?action=edit&section=17" title="Edit section's source code: Demo timer"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>In the <a href="/w/Demo_Mode" title="Demo Mode">demo mode</a>, a timer shows on the top-right indicating the remaining free playtime for that world.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Bedrock_Edition_exclusive_elements"><i>Bedrock Edition</i> exclusive elements</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?section=18&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Bedrock Edition exclusive elements" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?action=edit&section=18" title="Edit section's source code: Bedrock Edition exclusive elements"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Controller_hints">Controller hints</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?section=19&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Controller hints" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?action=edit&section=19" title="Edit section's source code: Controller hints"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>When using a controller, available actions the player can take are listed on the bottom left and right of the screen, alongside the icon of the button to press to perform that action.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Mobile_controller">Mobile controller</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?section=20&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Mobile controller" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?action=edit&section=20" title="Edit section's source code: Mobile controller"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">Main article: <a href="/w/Controls#Touch" title="Controls">Controls § Touch</a></div><div style="display: flex; align-items: center; float: right;">
<figure class="pixel-image" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/w/File:Joystick_control_mode.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="/images/thumb/Joystick_control_mode.png/246px-Joystick_control_mode.png?1de5b" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="246" height="146" class="mw-file-element" srcset="/images/thumb/Joystick_control_mode.png/492px-Joystick_control_mode.png?1de5b 2x" data-file-width="888" data-file-height="528"></a><figcaption>Joystick control mode</figcaption></figure>
<figure class="pixel-image" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/w/File:HUD-Bedrock-D_Pad_buttons.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="/images/thumb/HUD-Bedrock-D_Pad_buttons.png/260px-HUD-Bedrock-D_Pad_buttons.png?7c98b" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="260" height="120" class="mw-file-element" srcset="/images/thumb/HUD-Bedrock-D_Pad_buttons.png/520px-HUD-Bedrock-D_Pad_buttons.png?7c98b 2x" data-file-width="780" data-file-height="361"></a><figcaption>D-Pad control mode</figcaption></figure>
</div>
<p>These buttons are present only in mobile and desktop versions with a touchscreen, and they are used to control the player. Players can <a href="/w/Sneak" class="mw-redirect" title="Sneak">sneak</a>, fly and jump using the mobile controller.
</p><p>In the settings under <span class="t-ui">"Controls" → "Touch"</span>, players can choose between D-Pad, normal joystick (touch control mode), and joystick with crosshair aim control mode. D-Pad crosshair aim is available separate using "Split Controls" setting.
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/w/File:Customize_Touch_Controls_(Bedrock).png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="/images/thumb/Customize_Touch_Controls_%28Bedrock%29.png/300px-Customize_Touch_Controls_%28Bedrock%29.png?5800d" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="300" height="135" class="mw-file-element" srcset="/images/thumb/Customize_Touch_Controls_%28Bedrock%29.png/600px-Customize_Touch_Controls_%28Bedrock%29.png?5800d 2x" data-file-width="2400" data-file-height="1080"></a><figcaption>The control customization interface. Note that this does not show the top buttons.</figcaption></figure>
<p>The position, scale, and opacity of individual controls can be customized in the touch settings.
</p><p>In addition to control buttons, there is a row of static buttons at the top of the screen, allowing to change perspective (if enabled), open the <a href="/w/Game_Menu" title="Game Menu">game menu</a>, open the <a href="/w/Chat" title="Chat">chat</a>, and access <a href="/w/Emotes" class="mw-redirect" title="Emotes">emotes</a>. The size of these buttons can be adjusted.
</p><p>An independent action button sometimes appears above the hotbar when a unique action can be performed.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Paper_doll">Paper doll</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?section=21&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Paper doll" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?action=edit&section=21" title="Edit section's source code: Paper doll"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>The paper doll is a side-view of the player displayed in the top-left corner of the screen. It shows the player's <a href="/w/Skin" title="Skin">skin</a> and any <a href="/w/Armor" title="Armor">armor</a> worn. If the player is walking, the paper doll shows the player's legs moving. If the player is <a href="/w/Sneaking" title="Sneaking">sneaking</a>, sprint-<a href="/w/Swimming" title="Swimming">swimming</a>, <a href="/w/Emotes" class="mw-redirect" title="Emotes">emoting</a>, or flying with <a href="/w/Elytra" title="Elytra">elytra</a>, this can also be seen.
</p><p>The paper doll can be toggled by pressing <kbd class="key nowrap">F8</kbd> on keyboard, or in the <a href="/w/Settings" title="Settings">settings</a>. This can be done independently from hiding the HUD, although pressing <kbd class="key nowrap">F1</kbd> also disables the paper doll.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Position_and_Days_Played">Position and Days Played</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?section=22&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Position and Days Played" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?action=edit&section=22" title="Edit section's source code: Position and Days Played"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>If enabled in the <a href="/w/World_options" class="mw-redirect" title="World options">world options</a>, the player's <a href="/w/Coordinates" title="Coordinates">coordinates</a> and/or days played will be displayed in a box in the top left of the screen. If both are enabled at the same time, the position is listed above the number of days played. Both are shown below the paper doll, and above the chat. The background opacity of this text is affected by the "Text Background Opacity" accessibility setting.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Identify">Identify</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?section=23&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Identify" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?action=edit&section=23" title="Edit section's source code: Identify"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/w/File:Describe.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="/images/thumb/Describe.png/300px-Describe.png?c1e5a" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="300" height="169" class="mw-file-element" srcset="/images/thumb/Describe.png/600px-Describe.png?c1e5a 2x" data-file-width="3840" data-file-height="2160"></a><figcaption>A mob described above the hotbar after the button has been pressed.</figcaption></figure>
<p>In the <a href="/w/Controls" title="Controls">controls</a> menu, a keybind can be assigned to Identify for keyboard & mouse or controller modes. Once pressed in-game, this shows above the hotbar (as an item tooltip) the name of the <a href="/w/Block" title="Block">block</a> or <a href="/w/Entity" title="Entity">entity</a> the player currently faces. If an entity has been renamed, the custom name will display instead. This is only shown when an object in front of the player can be interacted with (usually hitting or breaking), so <a href="/w/Water" title="Water">water</a> or objects far away are not described.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Splitscreen">Splitscreen</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?section=24&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Splitscreen" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?action=edit&section=24" title="Edit section's source code: Splitscreen"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p><a href="/w/Splitscreen" title="Splitscreen">Splitscreen</a> mode on consoles divides the screen into sections for each player, each having its own HUD. The gamertag of the respective player is shown on the top-right of the HUD for each section, which can be toggled in the video settings.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Compass">Compass</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?section=25&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Compass" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?action=edit&section=25" title="Edit section's source code: Compass"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><span><video id="mwe_player_91" poster="/images/thumb/Directional_Compass.mp4/300px--Directional_Compass.mp4.jpg?3dd6d" preload="none" controls="" data-mw-tmh="" class="mw-file-element" width="300" height="169" playsinline="" data-durationhint="12" data-mwtitle="Directional_Compass.mp4" data-mwprovider="local" resource="/w/File:Directional_Compass.mp4"><source src="/images/Directional_Compass.mp4?3dd6d" type="video/mp4; codecs="avc1.64002A, mp4a.40.2""></video></span><a href="/w/File:Directional_Compass.mp4" class="mw-file-magnify"></a><figcaption>The <i>Editor</i>'s compass on the top-right</figcaption></figure>
<p>Available in the <i><a href="/w/Editor" class="mw-redirect" title="Editor">Editor</a></i> only, a compass shows on the top-right of the world viewer in tool mode. This rotates accordingly with the player's view, showing the increasing or decreasing directions of X and Z <a href="/w/Coordinates" title="Coordinates">coordinates</a>. Clicking on a direction of the compass turns the camera into that direction. It shows as part of the HUD in the actual world viewer; not as part of the GUI overlay from tool mode. It can be toggled in the settings.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Java_Edition_exclusive_elements"><i>Java Edition</i> exclusive elements</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?section=26&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Java Edition exclusive elements" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?action=edit&section=26" title="Edit section's source code: Java Edition exclusive elements"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/w/File:AttackIndicatorCrosshair.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="/images/AttackIndicatorCrosshair.png?98e78" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="90" height="60" class="mw-file-element" data-file-width="90" data-file-height="60"></a><figcaption>Attack indicator (when below the crosshair), empty and full</figcaption></figure><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/w/File:AttackIndicatorHotbar.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="/images/AttackIndicatorHotbar.png?10d3b" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="120" height="57" class="mw-file-element" data-file-width="120" data-file-height="57"></a><figcaption>Attack indicator (when next to the hotbar), empty and full</figcaption></figure>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Attack_indicator">Attack indicator</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?section=27&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Attack indicator" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?action=edit&section=27" title="Edit section's source code: Attack indicator"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">Main article: <a href="/w/Melee_attack#Attack_cooldown" title="Melee attack">Melee attack § Attack cooldown</a></div>
<p>The attack indicator represents the attack cooldown timer. It can be displayed next to the crosshair, beside the hotbar, or be hidden completely. This disappears when the cooldown is full. If the <a href="/w/Option" class="mw-redirect" title="Option">option</a> for the attack indicator is set to "Crosshair" mode, a fully cooled weapon is being held, and a mob or player is in range, the sword icon and an additional plus-sign (+) indicator is shown below the crosshair, indicating that the weapon is in range to land a full-damage blow.
</p><p>If the option for the attack indicator is set to "Hotbar" mode, the attack cooldown timer is indicated by a sword icon near the crosshair that fills, representing the cooldown progress. This sword icon disappears once the item is fully charged.
</p><p>In the <a href="/w/Java_Edition_Combat_Tests" title="Java Edition Combat Tests">combat tests</a>, a shield indicator can also be enabled in the same locations.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Debug_screen">Debug screen</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?section=28&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Debug screen" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?action=edit&section=28" title="Edit section's source code: Debug screen"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">Main article: <a href="/w/Debug_screen" title="Debug screen">Debug screen</a></div>
<p>The debug screen (also commonly referred to as the "F3 screen") is triggered when <kbd>F3</kbd> is pressed. It functions as a menu for accessing debugging information, but it also provides useful in-game information like <a href="/w/Coordinates" title="Coordinates">player coordinates</a>.
</p><p>The debug screen consists of info text lines and five toggleable graphs: profiler, frame rate, <a href="/w/Tick" title="Tick">tick</a> rate, bandwidth, and ping time graphs. These graphs can be toggled with specific key combinations.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="List_Players">List Players</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?section=29&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: List Players" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?action=edit&section=29" title="Edit section's source code: List Players"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">Main article: <a href="/w/Multiplayer#Player_list" title="Multiplayer">Multiplayer § Player list</a></div>
<p>In multiplayer, holding the key bound to List Players (default: <kbd class="key nowrap">↹ Tab</kbd>) will show a list of players at the middle of the top of the screen, including their <a href="/w/Username" class="mw-redirect" title="Username">username</a>, the front face of their <a href="/w/Skin" title="Skin">skin</a>'s head, and their signal strength.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Options">Options</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?section=30&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Options" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?action=edit&section=30" title="Edit section's source code: Options"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>In the <a href="/w/Options" title="Options">options</a> menu, the GUI scale option changes the size of the HUD and GUI. The number of the GUI scale is equivalent to The Pixels, one pixel of the original texture is upscaled to. The default setting, "auto", changes the size of the HUD and GUI depending on the size of the game window.‌<sup class="nowrap Inline-Template" title="">[<i><span title="This statement only applies to Java Edition"><a href="/w/Java_Edition" title="Java Edition">Java Edition</a>  only</span></i>]</sup>
</p><p>There is an option to hide the HUD. If the player is using keyboard controls, this can also be done with <kbd class="key nowrap">F1</kbd>. In <a href="/w/Bedrock_Edition" title="Bedrock Edition"><i>Bedrock Edition</i></a>, the "Hide HUD" option toggles the hotbar, crosshair, and if using touch controls, buttons. The hand, paper doll, and coordinates are separate options.
</p><p>In <a href="/w/Bedrock_Edition" title="Bedrock Edition"><i>Bedrock Edition</i></a>, the <code><span>/<a href="/w/Commands/hud" title="Commands/hud">hud</a></span></code> command can toggle the visibility of each HUD element.
</p><p>Players can toggle the HUD, the <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vignetting" class="extiw" title="wikipedia:Vignetting">vignette</a> effect on fancy graphics, some screen effects and overlays, and the block hitbox by pressing the <kbd class="key nowrap">F1</kbd> key.
</p><p>The player can choose whether to use their right or left hand. This option also moves the off-hand slot to the opposite side in <a href="/w/Java_Edition" title="Java Edition"><i>Java Edition</i></a>, and mirrors the touch controls in <a href="/w/Bedrock_Edition" title="Bedrock Edition"><i>Bedrock Edition</i></a>.
</p><p>In <i><a href="/w/Java_Edition" title="Java Edition">Java Edition</a></i>, the <a href="/w/Melee_attack#Attack_cooldown" title="Melee attack">attack indicator</a> can be set to show by the crosshair, beside the hotbar, or to have it hidden. In the <a href="/w/Java_Edition_Combat_Tests" title="Java Edition Combat Tests">combat tests</a>, a shield indicator can also be enabled in the same locations.
</p><p>In <i>Java Edition</i>, <a href="/w/Subtitles" class="mw-redirect" title="Subtitles">subtitles</a> can be enabled in the "Music & Sounds" or "Accessibility Settings" sections of the <a href="/w/Options" title="Options">options</a> menu.
</p><p>In <i>Java Edition</i>, <a href="/w/Toasts" title="Toasts">music toasts</a> can be disabled in "Music & Sounds".
</p><p>The <a href="/w/Autosave" title="Autosave">autosave</a> indicator can be toggled in the video settings.
</p><p>In <i>Java Edition</i>, various settings related to the <a href="/w/Chat" title="Chat">chat</a> can be modified in <a href="/w/Options" title="Options">options</a>. In <a href="/w/Bedrock_Edition" title="Bedrock Edition"><i>Bedrock Edition</i></a>, these settings can only be changed in the <a href="/w/Chat#Chat_settings" title="Chat">chat settings</a> accessible from the chat menu, except for the opacity and message duration, which can be changed in the <a href="/w/Settings#Accessibility" title="Settings">accessibility settings</a>.
</p><p>In <i>Bedrock Edition</i>, the opacity of several HUD elements can be changed in the accessibility settings, as well as toast notification duration.
</p><p>In <i>Bedrock Edition</i>, the UI style can be toggled between Classic and Pocket. Pocket UI (default on mobile) moves certain objects such as the health and hunger bar to the top corners of the screen.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="China_Edition"><i>China Edition</i></h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?section=31&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: China Edition" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Heads-up_display?action=edit&section=31" title="Edit section's source code: China Edition"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>

</div>
</div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/w/File:MCCN_Screenshot.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="/images/thumb/MCCN_Screenshot.png/300px-MCCN_Screenshot.png?4e250" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="300" height="136" class="mw-file-element" srcset="/images/thumb/MCCN_Screenshot.png/600px-MCCN_Screenshot.png?4e250 2x" data-file-width="2388" data-file-height="1080"></a><figcaption>The HUD in <i><a href="/w/China_Edition" title="China Edition">China Edition</a></i>.</figcaption></figure>
<p>In <i><a href="/w/China_Edition" title="China Edition">China Edition</a></i>, a "2 button" can be seen at the top of the screen. There is also a button to allow the player to take a screenshot or switch the camera and change voice settings.
</p><p>At the right of the screen, a button can be seen that is used to lock walking, sprinting or sneaking. It can be useful in some situations.
</p>
